failure.summary: A user-rejected candidate remains addressable as an immutable commit or closed PR and can later be silently reused, cherry-picked, copied, or treated as a baseline after the active branch has been restored.

independentObservations.rejectedReason: User rejected P03 C2 visual result and restored P02 C2 as the current knit lineage baseline.
User rejected R05 and restored R04 as the current brow-lash lineage baseline.

mustNeverRepeat: Treat an immutable rejected commit or closed PR as a valid production baseline because it remains fetchable.
Treat branch reset, PR closure, page similarity, or a renamed directory as proof that rejected content cannot return.
Cherry-pick, copy, regenerate, or indirectly inherit a rejected file/tree/behavior without explicit current user reauthorization.
Erase rejected evidence from history or claim that a published Git object was physically deleted.
Promote a restored lineage baseline to final visual acceptance merely because the user selected it as the restart point.
gate: A rejected candidate remains EVIDENCE_ONLY even when its immutable SHA or closed PR is readable.
A new candidate is HOLD_REJECTED_DESCENDANT_PRESENT when rejected ancestry or rejected content identity is present and no exact current user reauthorization covers it.
Ancestry checks are necessary but not sufficient: copied or regenerated rejected files must also be checked by path, tree/blob digest, or behavior-specific regression.
A clean descendant of the restored accepted baseline is only eligible for normal verification; it is not automatically reference-faithful, visually accepted, or production-ready.
Reauthorization must name the rejected element and scope; a general request to continue does not revive all rejected work.

activation.learningQuestion: How can copied or semantically regenerated rejected behavior be detected when Git ancestry and exact blob digests no longer match?
